Praying to the RNG Gods -- What is Chance's Place in Gaming?
You are knocking it out of the park with the interesting gaming posts today, /u/Dereliction. Neat stuff!

It's fascinating you mention this, because recently I became convinced that the RNG in Wizardry (1981) became broken when it got ported to DOS from the Apple II. After trying both versions, it's astounding how different they feel, purely off of how the RNG seems weighted in one vs the other.

I also recall Baldur's Gate got patched early on to fix the randomness in the attack rolls. Which is not to say they were broken, but people complained that they were too streaky, so they altered them to distribute more evenly and feel more fair.

Naturally, streaks are common in true randomness as anybody who's a fan of dice games can attest to. But sometimes it is more important for the game to feel "fair" instead of relying on true randomness. Which is why many people replaced the dice in Catan with a deck of 72 cards consisting of every possible die roll, twice.

Personally I posses the sort of temperament where excessive randomness in my games drives me absolutely insane.

Interesting read and there is a lot to say about the subject.

For example, even in competitive scenarios luck and even unfair elements could add a lot of welcome depth to the game.

Take for example, fighting games. Balance is extremely important, but surprisingly enough a perfectly balanced game is undesirable by developers because it removes the potential for "exceptional" performances and the unpredictable nature of a game.
